The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the ground part using deionized water as the dielectric fluid, with fine finish mode and automatic edge deburr enabled, producing a precision finished part that is transferred to a mobile robot, all for 78 minutes.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a lathed part using a pull-type spline broach to achieve a Class 6 fit, taking 76 minutes, after which the resulting broached component is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On the Gear Shaper, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 24 teeth using a shaping speed of 180 rpm, resulting in a shaped gear, and the operation takes 13 minutes before the component is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a Drill Press, a precision drilling operation is performed on the broached component for 12 minutes, creating holes with a diameter of 8.5 mm and a tolerance of ±0.01 mm, resulting in a finished part with holes that is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On a Screw Machines, Screw Threading is performed on a Lathed part for 23 minutes, creating M6 metric coarse threads at a production rate of 450 parts per hour, resulting in a Screwed component that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component loaded by a mobile robot, using a 3000 W laser with nitrogen gas assist at 18 bar and a cutting speed of 2.5 m/min, operating for 66 minutes to produce a cut sheet metal part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

A planed part is loaded from a conveyor belt onto a grinding machine where a surface grinding operation is performed using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 200 mm/min, resulting in a ground part that is then transferred to a mobile robot, all taking 30 minutes.

On the Vertical Lathe, a Finish Turning operation is performed on the Drilled component using a CNC programmed contouring toolpath with a precision level of ±0.008 mm, lasting for 66 minutes, transforming the input into the Final drilled and shaped part, which is then placed on the ConveyorBelt.

Using a Punch Press, a sheet metal component is punched with a 12 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 120 strokes per minute and automatically calibrated die alignment for 52 minutes, transforming it from a raw sheet metal on a conveyor belt into a finished cut sheet metal product that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Perform finish milling on a milled part using a horizontal milling machine at a milling speed of 750 rpm with a climb milling tool path covering the full profile to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, taking 67 minutes, where the input milled part is loaded from a mobile robot and the resulting finished machined component is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal fed from a conveyor belt, using a hardened steel, double-edged blade with a shear angle of 2.5° and a cutting speed of 1 cut every 15 seconds, processing for 42 minutes to produce sheared sheet metal that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a Bandsaw, a Metal bar is cut off through cut-off sawing for 91 minutes with a bi-metal blade of 4 TPI at a saw speed of 60 m/min and a cutting width of 3 mm kerf, resulting in a Lathed part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On the CNC Turning Center, a CNC turning operation is performed on a lathed part loaded from the ConveyorBelt, using CNC program #7A-22, with tool offsets automatically compensated via probe and a spindle speed of 720 rpm, lasting for 84 minutes, resulting in a finished machined component transferred to the MobileRobot.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs precision wire cutting on a ground part loaded from a MobileRobot, using fine finish mode, auto deburr settings, and deionized water as the dielectric fluid, producing a precision finished part that is placed on a ConveyorBelt, taking 94 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component located on the conveyor belt, using a 3000 watt laser with nitrogen gas assist at a cutting speed of 5 meters per minute for 7 minutes, resulting in a cut sheet metal part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

A horizontal milling operation is performed on a milled part using a horizontal milling machine at a milling speed of 1200 RPM with a climb milling tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, lasting for 40 minutes, after which the finished machined component is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a Punch Press, a sheet metal component is punched for 29 minutes to create a finished sheet metal product, with a 10 mm diameter punch, a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute, and automatic die centering, after which the cut sheet metal is transferred to a ConveyorBelt from the MobileRobot.

On a Drill Press, a metal bar is drilled using an 8 mm drill at a spindle speed of 900 RPM and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, producing a drilled component, which takes 87 minutes, with the input metal bar coming from a ConveyorBelt and the output drilled component placed on a MobileRobot.

On a CNC Turning Center, a CNC Turning operation is performed on a lathed part for 18 minutes, using CNC program Program_003 with an auto-measured tool offset and a spindle speed of 1500 RPM, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Broaching Machine, a metal bar is broached using a pull broach with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/tooth and a depth of cut of 5 mm, transforming it into a broached component that is then placed on a MobileRobot, and the operation runs for 82 minutes.

On a Screw Machines, screw threading is performed on a lathed part to create M10 metric coarse threads, processing at a rate of 120 units per hour, and the operation runs for 75 minutes, after which the screwed component is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The honing machine performs a honing operation on a honed cylinder to achieve a precise bore size of 25.4 mm using a grit size of 220, processing the part for 32 minutes, after which the precision finished part is transferred to a mobile robot.

A vertical milling operation is performed on a lathed part using a vertical milling machine for 45 minutes, employing an end mill tool at a milling speed of 1000 RPM and a depth of cut of 3 mm, resulting in a milled part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to vertical turning for 23 minutes, using a carbide insert tool at a rotation speed of 600 RPM and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

A milled part is shaped on a shaper using a high-speed steel tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute for 69 minutes, resulting in a shaped part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Gear Shaper, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 24 teeth through the gear shaping operation at a speed of 40 strokes per minute, lasting for 92 minutes, resulting in a shaped gear transported by a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a broached component is processed through gear hobbing for 29 minutes to produce a hobbied gear with an involute profile, using a hobbing speed of 60 RPM and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, after which the finished gear is transferred to a mobile robot.

The metal bar is cut using a bandsaw in a sawing operation lasting 37 minutes, with a bi-metal blade at a saw speed of 80 m/min and a cutting width of 3 mm, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding using a grinding machine equipped with an aluminum oxide grinding wheel rotating at 1800 m/min and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, transforming it into a ground part, which is then placed on a conveyor belt, all taking 8 minutes.

Using a Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut in a bandsaw cutting operation lasting 11 minutes, operating at a saw speed of 60 meters per minute with a bi-metal variable pitch blade and a cutting width of 3 mm kerf, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Gear Shaper, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with a 20-degree pressure angle and 36 teeth using a gear shaping operation at a speed of 180 strokes per minute, taking 4 minutes to complete, after which the resulting shaped gear is placed on a conveyor belt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to vertical turning for 34 minutes, using a carbide insert with TNMG 160408 geometry as the cutting tool, rotating the workpiece at 450 rpm with a feed rate of 0.2 mm per revolution, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Screw Machines, a screw threading operation is performed on a lathed part to create a metric coarse thread with M10 x 1.5 screw size, taking 14 minutes to complete, during which 120 parts per hour are produced, resulting in a screwed component that is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The horizontal milling machine performs a face milling operation using a staggered tooth cutter at a milling speed of 320 rpm to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm on the milled part, which is loaded from the mobile robot, and completes the machining process in 57 minutes, resulting in a finished machined component transferred to the conveyor belt.
